question: Can a memory get sharper from being used?
_rung_witness_comment: SHELL.md r5.2. GPSCoord's rule "any pending gate blocks live_deployed" is too blunt: independent_use is pending FOREVER by construction, so no surface could ever advance. So the record names WHICH gate witnesses the rung it claims, and the others stay pending without blocking it. install_matrix is the right one here: it probed every release asset the installer can ask for and found the linux-x64 archive at 200, which is exactly what live_deployed claims and all it claims. test_suite is approved too, but it witnesses the TREE, not the deployment.
_nav_breakpoint_comment: SHELL.md r6: the breakpoint belongs to the surface, not the shell, and it has to be MEASURED rather than computed. r5 published 430px, measured on a four-item nav. THIS NUMBER MOVED ONCE DURING THE SAME SESSION AND THE WAY IT MOVED IS THE POINT: it was first set to 560 from an arithmetic estimate (logo 114 + items and gaps 364 + .top gap 16 + .wrap padding 44 = 538, stack 22px above it), and then the r9 work renamed one nav item from Demos to Correct us. That widened the nav by 22px and pushed the real wrap point to 576, past the 560 set for it, so every width from 561 to 575 rendered an UNSTACKED header with a two-row nav — the exact defect the rule exists to prevent, reintroduced by a five-character label change. The estimate was wrong in the first place because flex-wrap distributes inside the nav element own allotted width rather than against the sum. Bisected in Chrome 2026-08-17: one row at 576, two rows at 575, so the breakpoint is 600 and stacks 24px before it. ANY CHANGE TO A NAV LABEL INVALIDATES THIS NUMBER AND IT MUST BE RE-BISECTED. Verified over 390/500/545/560/561/570/575/576/585/600/601/700/790/800/815/1000/1280/1600.
_ink_box_comment: SHELL.md r7, second item: a line-height set against the em size can be smaller than the font's actual ink, and consecutive lines then overlap — agentromatic's Syne h1 overlapped by 11.8px and a descender collided with the cap-height beneath it. MEASURED here rather than assumed, 2026-08-17 in Chrome at 1280, by rendering each element's own text in its own computed font to a canvas and comparing actualBoundingBoxAscent+actualBoundingBoxDescent against the computed line box. Space Grotesk 600 at 57.6px inks 51.0px inside a 60.5px box. Every value above is headroom in pixels and every one is positive, so nothing here needed changing. Re-measured at 390/700/1280/1600 for the h1: +4.1 / +5.2 / +9.5 / +9.5. THE PUBLICATION GATE CANNOT CHECK THIS — it has no font engine and no browser — so it is a recorded measurement, not an enforced law, and it is said that way on purpose.
_nav_labels_comment: The exact header nav, as it was when nav_breakpoint_px was bisected. The breakpoint is a function of these strings and nothing else, and a five-character rename is what invalidated it the first time — so the gate compares the artifact's nav against this list and refuses when they differ, which turns "re-bisect after touching a nav label" from a comment into a stop.
_cited_specs_comment: SHELL.md r5.3: every §N in the page's VISIBLE text must resolve to a real heading in the spec it cites. This page cites none — every § on this surface is in a source comment, and comments are not text a reader reads. The map is empty and the gate reports 0 citations rather than passing silently; the day a citation is written, the record has to name the file it points into or the build stops.
surface_rung_covers: one artifact — one npm package and one binary — graphonomous@0.4.2, and the single linux-x64 archive its install downloads

status.statement: graphonomous@[[published_version]] is on the public npm registry and installs on linux-x64. The engine in this repository is [[tree_version]], and it has never been published. The installer advertises [[install_targets_total]] platforms; [[install_targets_ok]] of them has a release asset.
status.source: mix test at graphonomous commit 5a9e00b; registry.npmjs.org/graphonomous dist-tags; an HTTP probe of every one of the [[install_targets_total]] release assets v[[published_version]] declares. Every figure on this page is emitted from records/witness.json, and check.mjs re-derives each one against the tree and the registry.
status.limit: The test count was measured on the [[tree_version]] tree in this repository, which is NOT the artifact npm serves — so [[tests_total]] passing is evidence about code you cannot install. Nothing here establishes that the published [[published_version]] binary passes those tests, that the engine is correct rather than merely green, or that anyone outside this machine has ever run it. The demo and benchmark pages elsewhere on this domain were not audited by this pass and are not covered by the rung above.

advance.requires: Someone who is not us installs it and reports a result — a filed issue, a benchmark run, or a fork. That is the only rung nobody here can award themselves. Publishing [[tree_version]], and building the missing platform binaries, is what would make it possible for most people to try.

contact._why_here_comment: This surface publishes an install matrix in which three of four platforms 404 and a ledger in which nobody has installed the published package on a clean machine and spoken MCP to it. A reader reporting that the linux-x64 tarball did or did not work is the shortest path this domain has to the external rung — the one rung nobody here can award themselves — so the form says that next to itself rather than being a generic contact box.
